Question: Is the 'ability to consummate' concept subject to Material Adverse Effect carveouts?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement Excerpt:
"'Consolidated Material Impact' shall mean any event, condition, change, or development that, individually or in combination with other events, would have a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, or operational capacity of the Company, including any factor that would prevent, materially delay, or impair the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. Notwithstanding the exceptions set forth herein, the following carveouts apply only to effects that are peripheral to the transaction consummation: (i) variations in general market conditions; (ii) fluctuations in currency exchange rates; and (iii) changes in broad-based credit or capital market conditions, provided that such events do not impose a disproportionate adverse effect relative to industry peers. Importantly, no event or circumstance that directly affects the Company's ability to consummate the transactions shall be excluded from being considered a Consolidated Material Impact, regardless of whether it falls within the aforementioned carveouts."

Question: Is the “ability to consummate” concept subject to Material Adverse Effect carveouts?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement: "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, or occurrence that, taken individually or in aggregate, would materially impair the financial condition or operating results of the Company, including events that would prevent, delay, or impair the Company’s ability to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for purposes of determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred, any effect attributable solely to: (i) fluctuations in general economic conditions, (ii) shifts in the global or U.S. financial markets, (iii) widespread industry trends or regulatory changes affecting all competitors on an equal basis, (iv) uniform modifications in GAAP or similar accounting standards, or (v) transient stock price volatility, shall be expressly excluded from consideration. Only impairments to consummation that arise from factors uniquely significant to the Company and disproportionate to its industry peers are to be considered under the Material Adverse Effect standard.
